entry.name: Seed-Start Grant SA
entry.summary: Matched grants for early-stage South Australian businesses commercialising an innovative product or service.
entry.eligibility: Australian-incorporated company with an active ABN; non-tax-exempt and GST-registered; turnover below A$1 million in each of the prior three financial years; based, or willing to be based, in South Australia before the project starts.
entry.limits: Seed grants are A$50,000–A$100,000 at a 2:1 government-to-applicant match. Start grants are A$100,001–A$500,000 at a 1:1 match. Defined commercialisation projects and a unique product or sustainable competitive advantage are required; confirm current round terms.

facts.Geography: Based, or willing to be based, in South Australia

provenance.evidence: The official business.gov.au programme page lists the grant as open, publishes both matched-funding bands and match ratios, and requires an Australian company with ABN and GST registration, turnover below A$1 million in each of the prior three financial years, and a South Australian base or commitment to relocate before project commencement.

entry.name: First Nations Innovation Acceleration Program QLD
entry.value: Investment grants up to A$100,000 plus advisory services
entry.summary: Funding and dedicated business advisory support for established Queensland First Nations businesses developing innovative products or services.
entry.eligibility: A First Nations-owned business that is established and operating in Queensland, developing an innovative product or service, and seeking advisory support and possible funding to accelerate that innovation.
entry.limits: Applications close 4 February 2027, or earlier if fully subscribed. The source describes support for mature, established businesses, so this is a scale-up pathway rather than an idea-stage startup grant.

facts.Eligibility: First Nations-owned, established and operating in Queensland
facts.Closing date: 4 February 2027; may close earlier if fully subscribed

provenance.evidence: The official business.gov.au listing shows the programme open to 4 February 2027, subject to earlier closure if fully subscribed, and specifies Queensland operation, First Nations ownership, an innovative product or service, grants up to A$100,000, and targeted advisory support for mature businesses.

entry.name: Regional Artificial Intelligence Initiative — British Columbia
entry.summary: Federal project funding for qualifying B.C. businesses commercialising AI or integrating AI into operations.
entry.eligibility: Incorporated business operating in British Columbia: commercialization projects require at least 1 year of operation and 1–500 FTE; AI adoption projects require at least 3 years and 5–500 FTE.
entry.limits: Applications close 23 November 2026 at 12:00 pm Pacific. Interest-free repayable contribution covers up to 50% of eligible project costs; at least 50% of project funding must be confirmed from non-government sources. Routine off-the-shelf AI purchases are excluded. Repayment typically starts one year after project completion and runs monthly for five years.

facts.Funding: Repayable; up to 50% of eligible costs

provenance.evidence: PacifiCan states this business intake is open through 12:00 pm Pacific on 23 November 2026. Incorporated B.C. businesses can seek C$200,000–C$5 million in interest-free repayable project contributions covering up to 50% of eligible costs. The who-can-apply and funding pages specify project-specific operating history and employee thresholds, at least 50% confirmed non-government co-funding, and repayment and cost restrictions.

entry.name: START — West of England
entry.org: TechSpark and West of England Mayoral Combined Authority
entry.value: Free 28-hour programme; possible funded incubator placement
entry.summary: Training, workshops and mentoring for people developing an early-stage technology business in the West of England.
entry.eligibility: Applicants must be over 18 and live in Bristol, South Gloucestershire or Bath and North East Somerset. For people with an idea, not yet trading, or within the first year of operating.
entry.limits: No new cohort dates are confirmed. The operator invites expressions of interest for future cohorts. A six-month funded incubator place is a possible outcome after pitching, not a guaranteed programme benefit.
entry.status: Future cohort dates unconfirmed; expressions of interest open

facts.Programme: 28 hours of learning, workshops and mentoring
facts.Location: Bristol, South Gloucestershire, or Bath and North East Somerset
facts.Next cohort: Dates not confirmed; expression of interest

provenance.evidence: TechSpark describes START as a free 28-hour early-stage technology founder programme for residents of Bristol, South Gloucestershire, or Bath and North East Somerset; it says future dates are not yet confirmed and offers an expression of interest. GOV.UK independently lists the programme for early-stage or first-year businesses in the West of England and describes the training, workshops, mentoring and opportunity to pitch for an incubator place.

entry.name: Pathways to Funding — North East England
entry.summary: Investor-readiness guidance for revenue-generating SMEs and innovation-driven businesses preparing to raise external finance.
entry.eligibility: A business or socially trading enterprise headquartered in Newcastle, Northumberland, or North Tyneside; aimed at revenue-generating SMEs and innovation-driven enterprises requiring external finance.
entry.limits: No grant or investment award is promised. Support includes workshops, one-to-one guidance, investor-readiness assessment and investor intelligence. GOV.UK lists start-ups with 1–2 years trading and established businesses; no closing date is stated.

facts.Support: Investor readiness workshops, one-to-one support, readiness levels, and investor intelligence

provenance.evidence: GOV.UK lists the programme as investor-readiness expertise and advice for businesses operating across Newcastle, Northumberland and North Tyneside, identifies start-ups with 1–2 years trading and established businesses, and was published 5 November 2026. UMi specifies that eligible organisations are headquartered in those areas, describes revenue-generating SMEs and innovation-driven enterprises needing external finance, and lists workshops, one-to-one support, readiness levels and investor intelligence. Neither source describes a guaranteed grant or investment award or a closing date.

entry.name: AI Decision-Making Visibility and Compliance Governance Challenge
entry.org: Innovative Solutions Canada / Shared Services Canada
entry.value: Phase 2 prototype contract up to C$2,000,000
entry.summary: Federal challenge seeking an AI governance solution that tracks decision processes, output traceability and alignment with Canadian government requirements.
entry.eligibility: Canadian-incorporated, for-profit small business with 499 or fewer FTEs, conducting R&D in Canada and meeting ISC’s Canadian workforce and executive residency thresholds. This challenge accepts Phase 2 proposals for solutions at TRL 5–9.
entry.limits: Proposals close 22 December 2026 at 14:00 Eastern. This is a competitive Phase 2 prototype development contract, not an unconditional grant; the challenge is restricted to prototype-ready solutions and final award decisions depend on evaluation and available funding. Review the solicitation before applying.
entry.status: Open for proposals until 22 December 2026, 14:00 Eastern

facts.Maximum contract: C$2,000,000 before applicable taxes and expenses

provenance.evidence: ISED’s challenge page identifies Shared Services Canada as sponsor, a contract mechanism, opening on 30 October 2026, closing on 22 December 2026 at 14:00 Eastern, and Phase 2-only applications for TRL 5–9 prototype development. It states the maximum Phase 2 contract is C$2,000,000. The official Challenge Stream page requires a for-profit Canadian-incorporated small business with no more than 499 FTEs, Canadian R&D, and specified Canadian wage, employee-place-of-work and senior-executive residency thresholds. Awards are competitive and subject to evaluation and funding availability.

entry.name: Female Founders Co-Investment Fund QLD
entry.summary: Queensland co-investment support for female-founded innovative businesses undertaking a pre-seed or seed capital raise.
entry.eligibility: Business headquartered and operating in Queensland with an active ABN and GST registration; at least 51% female-owned and female-led for at least six months; no more than 50 full-time-equivalent employees (FTEs), and not part of a group exceeding 50 FTEs. The business needs an innovative product beyond proof of concept and an investment plan or existing eligible investment offer.
entry.limits: Applications are open until 30 June 2027 or earlier if all funds are allocated. Funding supports a new pre-seed or seed raise; previous capital raises above A$500,000 disqualify. Confirm the required eligible-investor match and current round terms before applying.
entry.status: Open until 30 June 2027 or funds allocated

facts.Ownership and leadership: At least 51% female-owned and a woman in a primary executive role for at least six months

provenance.evidence: The official business.gov.au listing marks the fund open with a 30 June 2027 closing date and says applications may close once funds are allocated. It lists funding of A$50,000–A$200,000, Queensland head-office and operating-location requirements, an active ABN and GST registration, 51% female ownership and female executive leadership for at least six months, a maximum of 50 FTEs, and exclusion of businesses whose previous capital raises exceed A$500,000. Applicants must pursue an eligible pre-seed or seed raise and have an innovative product beyond proof of concept, a growth plan and an investment plan or offer.

entry.name: Ignite Program NT
entry.value: A$2,000 planning voucher or up to A$15,000 for MVP/commercialisation
entry.summary: Northern Territory mentoring and pre-seed support through planning and competitive MVP-development streams.
entry.eligibility: Legal entity with a valid ABN that qualifies as a Territory Enterprise and is not an excluded applicant. Stream A is for an innovative idea addressing a market need with commercial potential. Stream B requires an Innovation Project Plan or equivalent, an eligible project budget and demonstrated delivery capacity.
entry.limits: Stream A: up to A$2,000 ex GST, paid to an approved Innovation Partner, first-come-first-served from a A$100,000 pool while funds remain; complete the plan within 3 months. Stream B: up to A$15,000 ex GST, competitive and subject to available funding, with up to 6 months to deliver. Excludes government agencies and controlled bodies, statutory corporations, schools/universities/other educational institutions, and applicants failing grant terms. Stream B cannot cover retrospective costs, ordinary operating costs, unrelated work, debt, land/buildings, expenses before approval or activities already funded by another government programme. Stream B Round 2 closes 30 November 2026; check the official page for later rounds.
entry.status: Stream A year-round; Stream B Round 2 closes 30 November 2026

facts.Stream A: Up to A$2,000 voucher paid to approved Innovation Partner
facts.Stream B: Up to A$15,000 ex GST, competitive

provenance.evidence: The business.gov.au listing marks Ignite Program NT open and describes A$2,000 Stream A vouchers and Stream B support up to A$15,000. The NT Government page says Stream A is open year-round and Stream B Round 2 closes 30 November 2026. Guidelines dated 18 June 2026 specify legal entity, valid ABN, Territory Enterprise and exclusions; Stream A's A$100,000 pool and first-come allocation; Stream B's competitive assessment, delivery periods and ineligible costs. Awards are not guaranteed.

entry.name: Carbon Innovation Grants Program — Round 3
entry.org: Government of Western Australia — Department of Water and Environmental Regulation
entry.value: Feasibility: A$50,000–A$500,000 (up to 50%); pilot/capital works: A$100,000–A$1.5 million (up to 25%)
entry.summary: Competitive Western Australian grants for heavy-industry carbon-abatement or sequestration feasibility studies, pilot projects and capital works.
entry.eligibility: Applicant must have an ABN, GST registration, meet an eligible Australian entity type and fit-and-proper requirements. Project must be located in WA, or a feasibility study must be specific to WA sites; be new; support carbon abatement or sequestration and commercial viability; include at least one industrial business partner contributing cash or eligible in-kind support; and meet round and project timing rules.
entry.limits: Round 3 closes 11 December 2026 at 5pm AWST; around A$3.1 million is available. Existing projects already underway, business-as-usual activity, generic research not tied to heavy-industry facilities, projects without a WA site/location, renewable generation not directly supplying heavy industry on the same site, projects without an industrial business partner are ineligible, and projects intending to generate carbon credits outside WA or using methods ineligible under the Climate Active Carbon Neutral Standard are ineligible. Funding is competitive, paid by milestone in arrears, and is not guaranteed.

facts.Location: Western Australia: project site or WA-specific feasibility study
facts.Feasibility studies: A$50,000–A$500,000, up to 50% of eligible costs
facts.Pilot projects and capital works: A$100,000–A$1.5 million, up to 25% of eligible costs
facts.Industrial partner: At least one industrial business partner with cash or eligible in-kind contribution

provenance.evidence: The WA Government program page (last updated 7 October 2026) says Round 3 opened 10 September and closes 11 December 2026 at 5pm AWST, with around A$3.1 million available. It lists feasibility grants of A$50,000–A$500,000 capped at 50% of eligible costs, and pilot/capital-works grants of A$100,000–A$1.5 million capped at 25%. Applicants need an ABN, GST registration, eligible Australian entity status and fit-and-proper management. Projects must be in WA or, for feasibility studies, specific to WA locations; be new, aligned to carbon abatement/sequestration, commercially viable, include an industrial business partner contributing cash or eligible in-kind support, and meet timeframes. The WA page excludes existing or business-as-usual projects, generic research, projects without WA sites, renewable generation not directly supplying heavy industry on the same site, and projects without an industrial partner. Round 3 guidance documents page was last updated 4 November 2026. Awards are competitive; project and partner requirements do not establish endorsement or an existing partnership. It also excludes projects intending to generate carbon credits outside WA or using methods not eligible under the Climate Active Carbon Neutral Standard.
